subject: MX-style switch exploded cross-section — keycap lifted above a top housing shell, stem crown poking through the housing's crown opening, stem shaft descending through a slotted foam pad wrapped around the shaft at mid-housing height, spring coils beneath the pad seated on the bottom housing floor, contact leaves at the floor, and a PCB strip below.
motif: single switch cross-section, exploded vertical tiers, foam washer around stem shaft
notes: Deliberately distinct placement from the two nearest family pieces: pe-foam-mod.svg puts its foam layer at the plate/PCB gap (full-width case-level sheet, coral splash); o-ring-mod.svg puts its callout ring at the keycap-stem/standoff interface (bare-PCB top-down view, ochre splash). This piece is a single switch's exploded cross-section — the foam pad is a small slotted washer centered around the stem shaft mid-housing, seated directly atop the spring coils, matching the wire/foam-in-housing mechanism the article describes rather than either reference's location. Splash hue chosen as dusty rose (oklch(0.66 0.085 12)) specifically to avoid collision with pe-foam-mod's coral and o-ring-mod's ochre, per brief. Background is warm-paper (#F9F4EF) with a dark warm-grey stroke (#4A4540) rather than the family's on-dark warm-grey stroke convention, so the piece stays legible in light mode per the bearings.md directive. Bronze theme dot at upper-right per family ornamental convention; bronze bracket + leader callout labels the foam pad. Dashed explode-gap ticks mark the keycap-to-housing and housing-to-PCB separations consistent with the family's exploded-view language (see beginners-switch-buying-guide.svg, buckling-spring-deep-dive.svg).
